findings.problem: The stated design is internally inconsistent: it says the whole-file budget becomes a time, rather than memory, limit and that large images no longer consume it, but step 2 retains a budget on total decoded bytes. A total-output cap is neither a time limit nor an exemption for large images, so the specified change can still produce the false `scan_incomplete` alarm.
findings.suggestion: Specify one consistent resource model: for example, a separate wall-clock/decompression-work bound plus bounded per-piece memory, with an explicit rule for whether recognized large images count toward any cumulative output limit. Make the fixtures and expected caveats test that rule.

findings.location: docs/plans/2026-11-06-scan-false-alarms.md:67; 127-141; 160 (completion criterion 1, Increment C, and Increment D)
findings.problem: The required final result for arXiv 2005.14165 conflicts when optional Increment C runs. Criterion 1 requires only `large_image_streams`, while C deliberately adds `pattern_in_binary_data` for this exact `/JS(` case. D relaxes this only to 'no `javascript`', leaving the completion criterion unmet and the expected comparison ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: State separate, complete expected caveat sets for the B-only and B-plus-C paths, then use those same sets in the completion criteria and Increment D comparison.

findings.location: docs/plans/2026-11-06-scan-false-alarms.md:69-70; 110-114 (completion criterion 3 and Increment B test step 1)
findings.problem: The performance and memory checks are not reproducible acceptance criteria. 'Peak memory recorded' and memory that 'does not grow with their number' have no measurement method, baseline, file-size control, or threshold; a scan necessarily has memory that varies with its input size. Consequently the plan cannot establish whether it met its claimed resource-safety outcome.
findings.suggestion: Define the measurement tool and environment, hold total input size constant when varying image count (or state the allowed growth), and set numeric peak-memory and runtime limits derived from Increment A.

summary: The plan is directionally compatible with the pipeline spec, but its core budget semantics, optional-C completion state, and resource acceptance tests need resolution before it can be relied on.
